en.title: Real-Time CDC Analytics Pipeline
en.subtitle: From operational PostgreSQL changes to analytics-ready layers
en.summary: A runnable CDC stack that captures PostgreSQL WAL changes with Debezium, normalizes events in Python, and publishes analytics-ready bronze, silver, and gold layers with dbt and Streamlit.
en.businessProblem: Operational teams needed fresher analytics without buying a heavy black-box ELT layer. The real risk was solving latency by adding a stack nobody could explain, test locally, or evolve safely once schemas changed.
technicalSolution: Capture row-level PostgreSQL WAL changes through Debezium and Kafka Connect
Normalize Debezium envelopes and apply safe UPSERT behavior in a Python consumer
Persist replicated records in a target PostgreSQL before modeling bronze, silver, and gold layers with dbt
Expose pipeline freshness and analytical outputs in a lightweight Streamlit dashboard
en.architectureSummary: The flow is explicit end to end: PostgreSQL source -> Debezium -> Kafka -> Python consumer -> PostgreSQL target -> dbt -> Streamlit. That keeps CDC inspectable instead of magical, which is exactly the point of the case.
impact: Turns CDC from an abstract idea into a runnable path from source database to business-facing dashboard
Shows the tradeoff between a transparent local-first architecture and heavier managed ELT products
Creates proof for roles that need streaming, dbt layering, and operational analytics in the same story
en.body:
## What this case proves

This is not a slide about streaming. It is a full path you can inspect, run, and explain in an interview or architecture review. The project captures PostgreSQL changes from WAL, publishes them into Kafka through Debezium, normalizes payloads in Python, and only then promotes the data into dbt layers that analytics teams can trust.

## Why the design matters

The strongest decision in this repo is transparency. Instead of hiding transformation logic inside an opaque connector, the consumer owns coercion and UPSERT behavior. That makes the data movement easier to test, easier to reason about, and easier to extend when business rules change.

## Tradeoffs worth calling out

The stack is intentionally local-first. It uses Docker Compose, a target PostgreSQL, and Streamlit so the operating pattern stays visible. That is great for proof and learning, but in production you would likely add schema registry, lag monitoring, stronger secret handling, and managed scheduling.

## Practical takeaway

If the business problem is stale operational analytics, this case shows a credible middle path: fresher data without pretending every company needs a heavyweight platform from day one.

pt.title: Pipeline Analitico de CDC em Tempo Real
pt.subtitle: Das mudancas no PostgreSQL operacional ate camadas analiticas prontas
pt.summary: Um stack de CDC executavel que captura mudancas do WAL do PostgreSQL com Debezium, normaliza eventos em Python e publica camadas bronze, silver e gold com dbt e Streamlit.
pt.businessProblem: Times operacionais precisavam de analytics mais fresco sem comprar uma camada pesada e opaca de ELT. O risco real era reduzir latencia adicionando um stack que ninguem conseguiria explicar, testar localmente ou evoluir com seguranca quando o schema mudasse.
technicalSolution: Captura de mudancas linha a linha do WAL do PostgreSQL com Debezium e Kafka Connect
Normalizacao dos envelopes do Debezium e aplicacao de UPSERT seguro em um consumidor Python
Persistencia dos registros replicados em um PostgreSQL alvo antes da modelagem bronze, silver e gold com dbt
Exposicao da frescura do pipeline e dos outputs analiticos em um dashboard leve com Streamlit
pt.architectureSummary: O fluxo fica explicito de ponta a ponta: PostgreSQL origem -> Debezium -> Kafka -> consumidor Python -> PostgreSQL destino -> dbt -> Streamlit. Isso deixa o CDC inspecionavel em vez de magico, e esse e o valor central do caso.
impact: Transforma CDC de conceito abstrato em caminho executavel do banco de origem ate um dashboard de negocio
Mostra o tradeoff entre uma arquitetura transparente e local-first e alternativas gerenciadas mais pesadas
Cria prova para vagas e projetos que exigem streaming, camadas dbt e analytics operacional na mesma narrativa
pt.body:
## O que este caso prova

Isto nao e um slide sobre streaming. E um caminho completo que voce consegue inspecionar, executar e explicar em uma entrevista ou review de arquitetura. O projeto captura mudancas do PostgreSQL a partir do WAL, publica os eventos no Kafka via Debezium, normaliza payloads em Python e so depois promove os dados para camadas dbt em que analytics consegue confiar.

## Por que o desenho importa

A melhor decisao deste repo e a transparencia. Em vez de esconder a logica de transformacao dentro de um conector opaco, o consumidor assume coercao e UPSERT. Isso deixa a movimentacao mais facil de testar, de entender e de estender quando a regra de negocio muda.

## Tradeoffs que valem destacar

O stack e intencionalmente local-first. Usa Docker Compose, PostgreSQL destino e Streamlit para manter o padrao operacional visivel. Isso e excelente para prova e aprendizado, mas em producao o natural seria adicionar schema registry, monitoramento de lag, segredos mais fortes e agendamento gerenciado.

## Takeaway pratico

Se o problema de negocio e analytics operacional defasado, este caso mostra um caminho credivel: dados mais frescos sem fingir que toda empresa precisa de uma plataforma gigante no dia um.
